source.title: Residual Paving: Diagnosing the Routing Bottleneck in Selective Refusal Editing

record.tranche_reason: The study tests one-direction activation-steering controls under a selective-refusal protocol, including a DIM-style refusal direction, but does not reproduce the original all-layer, all-position projection intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper's main Residual Paving results are not rows because they do not apply or measure the claim's single difference-in-means refusal direction. The relevant results are the matched-bucket one-direction steering controls in Table 18. The paper describes their edit target as a designated safe-reframe behavior, not direct harmful compliance.
record.test_reason: Same-protocol baselines apply refusal-direction steering and ablation to instruct models and report refusal rates. Table 18 has a DIM-style benign-keep minus harmful-keep direction on Gemma-3-4B-IT. Tables 11-12 report local 'Refusal direction ablation/ActAdd' runs on about ten backbones, including Qwen3-4B-Thinking. The setting differs from the original: the edit target is safe-reframe non-refusal, judged by small LLM judges.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that one-direction steering, including a DIM-style refusal direction, cannot solve the selective three-way edit task, so routed residual editing is needed; the remaining harmful-keep loss is a routing problem. They make no claim about whether a single direction mediates refusal globally.
record.recipe_differences: The evaluated DIM-style direction is a benign-keep minus harmful-keep boundary direction, and the other primary control is an edit-target ActAdd direction. These are activation-steering comparators, not the original difference-in-means refusal-direction ablation at every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported steering outcomes vary with model and route condition in the non-primary ActAdd adaptations; primary Gemma comparator edit-refusal rates are unchanged by veto or oracle routing.

fits_no_version.finding: An edit-target ActAdd direction (safe-reframe minus refusal state) only partly reduces refusal on Gemma-3. It nearly eliminates refusal on Qwen when oracle-gated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A target-behaviour steering direction can replace refusal with a specific alternative response.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says an anonymous review artifact includes code; the public repository URL is pending)
record.problems: The comparator task's edit bucket consists of base-refused prompts paired with safe-reframe targets, not direct harmful-compliance requests. The matched primary comparator block reports no uncertainty intervals, and the non-primary comparator block does not state no-intervention edit-refusal baselines.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 11–13 and the broader external-method context tables contain additional comparator grids and derived summaries, but were not extracted as separate rows because they are presented as cross-paper method context rather than the matched one-direction controls highlighted as the direct test in Table 18.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; broad capability benchmarks.
Everything beyond one Qwen3-4B-Thinking comparator row set.

missing.what: Per-backbone local 'Refusal direction ablation' and 'Refusal direction ActAdd' edit ASR, harmful-keep ASR and benign preservation vs no intervention, for Gemma-3-4B, Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B/14B, Phi-4-mini, Qwen3-4B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B-Thinking, under two judges.
Local DIM runs at scale 1: Gemma-3-4B target success 10.0, Llama-3-8B 93.3 with benign retention 26.1.

record.verdict_notes: rows_left_out wrongly treats Tables 11-12 as cross-paper context: they are local same-dataset runs of refusal-direction ablation and bear directly on V1 and V8. The study's goal is selective editing, so global refusal loss on harmful keeps is consistent with V1, not against it. Edit success measures safe-reframe non-refusal judged by Phi-4-mini or Qwen2.5-7B, and the external-method pipelines are adaptations, not exact reproductions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests DIM-style and edit-target one-direction steering on designated safe-reframe edit prompts. Does not test the original harmful-minus-harmless direction projected out at every layer and position, adding that direction to induce refusal on harmless requests, or general capability preservation beyond the reported benign/harmful distribution-preservation measures.
Does not test jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation.
Does not test affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
Does not test whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded.
Does not test transfer of the same direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not test how refusal-training choices determine whether a single removable direction exists.
Does not test the original single-direction claim in reasoning models.

relationships.condition: Gemma-3-4B-IT, DIM-style direction at a preservation-constrained scale (Table 18)

relationships.display_finding: Edit refusal fell only from 100.0 to 78.9, while harmful refusal remained nearly unchanged.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Gemma-3-4B-IT, DIM-style direction at a preservation-constrained scale (Table 18)
source_check.reason: Table 18, DIM-style direction at s=8: edit refusal 100.0->78.9, harmful refusal 55.3->52.6, benign preservation 99.8. Veto and oracle variants also leave edit refusal at 78.9. This is a small move in the right direction at a chosen scale, so partial. Table 18 base rates come from a comparator export protocol, not the 500/500/98 split.

relationships.condition: Refusal-direction ablation on Gemma-2-2B-IT, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen3-4B-Instruct (Table 11, text-based, no rows)
relationships.reason: From the text: edit non-refusal rises from about 0-3% to about 60-75%, harmful-keep ASR rises similarly, and benign label agreement stays at or above 96%.
relationships.display_finding: Non-refusal on prompts targeted for refusal removal rose from approximately 0–3% to 60–75%, attack success on harmful prompts intended to retain refusal rose similarly, and benign label agreement remained at least 96%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Refusal-direction ablation on Gemma-2-2B-IT, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen3-4B-Instruct (Table 11, text-based, no rows)
source_check.reason: Removal is incomplete and depends on the judge and the objective grid. Table 11 (Phi/Qwen judge): Gemma-2 74.6/74.2, Llama-3-8B 75.4/68.6, Qwen2.5-1.5B 60.8/45.2, Qwen3-4B-Inst 65.2/57.8, so 25-55% of edit prompts are still refused. Table 12 (3-obj) for the same models: Llama-3-8B 34.8/23.2, Qwen2.5-1.5B 25.2/14.4, Gemma-2 75.0/57.6, Qwen3-4B-Inst 66.8/59.2. The verdict uses only Table 11 with the Phi judge. Benign label agreement of at least 96% is correct.

relationships.condition: Refusal-direction ablation on Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B (Tables 11-12, text-based); also benign pairwise non-worse ~57% across the grid
relationships.reason: From the text: removal is incomplete, with edit non-refusal of about 26-60% depending on judge and objective. Benign pairwise utility is non-worse than no intervention only ~57% of the time (Table 9).
relationships.display_finding: Edit non-refusal reached about 26–60%, depending on judge and objective, while benign pairwise utility matched or exceeded no intervention only about 57% of the time.

source_check.reason: Qwen2.5-7B: 39.0/26.0 (2-obj), 60.4/46.4 (3-obj). Qwen2.5-14B: 50.2/35.6, 59.2/42.2. Base is 1.4-7.0. So the 26-60% range is right. Pairwise NW 56.6 (Table 9) is a mean over the whole three-objective grid, not specific to these two models.

relation.reason: The study reports its own refusal rates for refusal-direction ablation and DIM-style steering on about nine backbones (Tables 11, 12, 18), so its results bear on whether ablating the direction removes refusal. It is not just a use of the direction as a tool.

tranche.reason: Different method and measure from the original. The main DIM-style control is a benign-keep minus harmful-keep direction added at scale s, not projected out (Table 7, Table 18). The Table 11-12 'Refusal direction ablation' rows are local comparator adaptations on base-refused SALAD-Bench edit prompts, scored by Phi-4-mini and Qwen2.5-7B judges, and the text does not describe how they were implemented. Their results bear on V1 and V8.

source_check.notes: The pack had none of the record's 12 rows to check. Table 18 values move in 2.6-pt steps, suggesting about 38 prompts per bucket (inferred; n not stated). Not covered by any verdict: Table 8 DIM scale-1 rows (Llama-3-8B: 93.3 target success but benign 26.1 and harmful preservation 3.6; Gemma-2-2B and Qwen2.5-14B: 0.0). The text does not define two- vs three-objective for the comparators.

statements.correction: Optional context: with the Qwen2.5-7B judge, Qwen3-4B-Thinking goes 3.4->28.2 (2-obj) and 3.4->1.4 (3-obj, below no-intervention). Cross-backbone sweeps decode only 32 tokens, and the text does not say how thinking traces were handled.
statements.problem: None. Numbers match Table 11 (2-obj, Phi-4 mini judge: Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 refusal-direction ablation 8.6->38.4) and Table 12 (3-obj, Phi-4 mini judge: 8.6->13.0). Non-reasoning Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 is 2.6->65.2 and 2.6->66.8. The 3-objective value is also from the Phi judge, which the statement leaves implicit.
